name: commuting_pauli_cluster_diagonalization
precondition: family dv_angle (Clifford+Rz op list, no Toffoli/CCZ, measurement-free); needs `rotations` and `nonclifford_rz`; 2 <= n_qubits <= 14 (so `v4.api.sim.unitary` can certify a cluster window). Requires at least 2 rotations whose front-frame Pauli axes coincide, i.e. len(frames(ops)) > number of distinct axis keys. On hhl_8: 475 rotations over 142 axis classes, so it triggers.
identity: Write the circuit, via `v4.api.pauli.frames`, as an ordered product of signed Pauli exponentials times a residual Clifford: C = W * prod_j exp(-i theta_j P_j / 2). Partition the ORDERED list P_1..P_m greedily into consecutive maximal clusters S_1,...,S_r such that the Paulis inside each cluster pairwise commute. Inside a cluster all factors commute, so they may be permuted freely and every pair with the same axis key merges (theta_i + s*theta_j, one rotation deleted, s = relative sign). Then, for each cluster, find a Clifford U_t that SIMULTANEOUSLY diagonalizes all of its Paulis: the cluster's Paulis span an isotropic (self-commuting) subspace of the symplectic space, so Gaussian elimination over GF(2) on the (x|z) tableau gives U_t built from H, S and CX with U_t P U_t^dag = +-Z_{m} for every member. Each exponential becomes a diagonal CNOT+Rz phase-polynomial term with affine parity label `labels()`; equal labels in the cluster merge again (`v4.api.phasepoly.equal_label_pairs`), and the resulting diagonal block is re-emitted as a parity-network CNOT ladder carrying one Rz per DISTINCT label. The cluster is emitted as U_t^dag (diagonal block) U_t; U_t^dag U_{t+1} is fused as a single Clifford between consecutive clusters and the trailing W is appended, so no Clifford cost is duplicated.
correctness: (1) `frames` is an exact rewriting: conjugating a Z-rotation through a Clifford prefix gives exp(-i theta (C^dag P C)/2), so the ordered exponential product times the residual Clifford equals the original circuit up to global phase. (2) If [P_i, P_j] = 0 then exp(-i a P_i/2) and exp(-i b P_j/2) commute exactly, so permutation within a cluster is an identity; and exp(-i a P/2) exp(-i b (sP)/2) = exp(-i (a + s b) P/2) since P^2 = I, which is the merge. (3) A set of pairwise-commuting Paulis generates an abelian subgroup, i.e. an isotropic subspace under the symplectic form; the Clifford group acts transitively on isotropic subspaces, so a Clifford U_t with U_t P U_t^dag in {+-Z-type} for all members exists and is produced constructively by symplectic Gaussian elimination. (4) Diagonal exponentials of Z-type Paulis are phase-polynomial terms; two terms with equal affine parity label are the same function of the computational basis state and add, and `v4.api.phasepoly.witness` proves the re-emitted parity network equals the diagonal block in O(ops) with no matrices. Every step is exact up to global phase; the frozen judge re-checks each cluster window with exact D[omega] when both sides are Clifford+T and phase-aligned operator distance otherwise.
trigger: Compute R = frames(ops). Walk R in order building consecutive maximal pairwise-commuting clusters (a record joins the open cluster iff its Pauli commutes with every Pauli already in it, else it opens a new cluster). Emit one match per cluster that (a) contains at least two records sharing an axis key, OR (b) contains at least two records whose labels coincide after diagonalization, i.e. the cluster's distinct-label count is strictly less than its record count. Clusters with no collapse are not matched, so they cost nothing. Each match carries the cluster's record positions, so `apply` rewrites exactly the op range it owns.
expected_effect: Deletes off-grid Rz gates: hhl_8 has 475 non-Clifford rotations but only 142 distinct front-frame Pauli axis classes, and the floor's merge rules could only fire when the later Pauli commuted with EVERY intervening rotation Pauli - a sequential condition that fails here (foldable_remaining = 0 while 333 same-axis duplicates survive). Clustering replaces that sequential test with a cluster-local one: within a commuting cluster the order is free, so same-axis duplicates merge even though they do not commute with rotations outside the cluster, and simultaneous diagonalization collapses a second group of rotations whose front-frame axes differ but whose diagonal parity labels coincide. Each deleted off-grid rotation removes one gridsynth call, currently ~59 T at eps_rz = 2.1e-6, and shrinking N_Rz also raises eps_rz for the survivors, making each remaining rotation slightly cheaper. The added Clifford cost (U_t, U_t^dag, parity ladders) is CNOT/H/S only and is free in T; cost order is lexicographic with T first, so it is paid in the third key only. I expect roughly a third of the 333 same-axis duplicates to land inside a single commuting cluster (hhl_8's rotations come from controlled-e^{iAt} Trotter blocks whose Pauli terms are largely mutually commuting within a block) plus a smaller label-collapse contribution: ~100-110 rotations removed.
source: E. van den Berg and K. Temme, 'Circuit optimization of Hamiltonian simulation by simultaneous diagonalization of Pauli clusters', Quantum 4, 322 (2020); simultaneous-diagonalization construction as in Aaronson-Gottesman (symplectic Gaussian elimination) and parity-network emission as in Amy, Azimzadeh, Mosca, 'On the controlled-NOT complexity of controlled-NOT-phase circuits' (2018).
